legacy_root.question: In a generated architecture the generator and its templates are a code-execution supply-chain node: specify who may modify them, how a malicious template edit would be detected BEFORE it ships (review scope, signing, hash pinning), and whether every generated artifact must carry provenance back to its registry entry plus the generator version that produced it.

scenario.catching_architecture: [REDACTED] output-fingerprint pin gate ([REDACTED]/gate.py) against pins/output-fingerprint.json, authorized by [REDACTED]-security-reviewer and [REDACTED]-[REDACTED]
scenario.on_this_estate: Live generate() writes 10 files. Planted edit changed 10/10 and the pin tripped. Whitespace did not trip the pin. Missing pin fail-closed. DESIGN control-plane/[REDACTED] generator path is absent; the named template file is [REDACTED]/generator.py.
procedure: 1. Copy [REDACTED] generator.py, registry.json, and registry.schema.json into a scratch directory (clone analogue; live tree untouched).
2. generate() the live registry; pin sha256 of every output plus tree_sha256; require authorized_by both reviewers.
3. Plant a semantic provenance() edit (generator_id suffix) that changes every generated file; run gate.py against the original pin.
4. On a second scratch copy, insert whitespace-only Python outside string literals; generate(); assert the output pin is silent while generator.py source hash would trip.
5. Delete the pin input; assert the gate fail-closes (pin-absent), not a vacuous pass.
6. Parse provenance on every live generated file and require registry_id and generator_version.
